{{short description|Belgian mathematician}}

[[Image:Jan Denef.jpg|thumb|Jan Denef]]
'''Jan Denef''' (born 4 September 1951) is a [[Belgium|Belgian]] [[mathematician]]. He is an Emeritus Professor of Mathematics at the [[KU Leuven|Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]] (KU Leuven).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wis.kuleuven.be/algebra/members|title=Section of Algebra members at KU Leuven}}</ref>

Denef obtained his [[PhD]] from KU Leuven in 1975 with a thesis on [[Hilbert's tenth problem]]; his advisors were Louis Philippe Bouckaert and Willem Kuijk.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=90814}}</ref>

He is a specialist of [[model theory]], [[number theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]]. He is well known for his early work on Hilbert's tenth problem and for developing the theory of [[motivic integration]] in a series of papers with [[François Loeser]]. He has also worked on [[computational number theory]].

Recently he proved a conjecture of [[Jean-Louis Colliot-Thélène]] which generalizes the [[Ax–Kochen theorem]].

In 2002 Denef was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|Invited Speaker]] at the [[International Congresses of Mathematicians]] in [[Beijing]].  His [[h-index|Hirsch-index]] is 24.
